data.gender_notes: Devabhay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit, ‘Deva’ meaning god and ‘bhay’ meaning fearless. This name is believed to be bestowed upon a child who is brave and fearless, instilling confidence in the face of adversity. The name Devabhay carries the meaning “God Fearless” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devabhay usually hope their child will grow to embody god fearless and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the divine fearlessness, Devabhay is a name that inspires courage and strength.
data.etymology: Devabhay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God Fearless.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devabhay total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Devabhay is mentioned in the Skanda Purana, a 6th-7th century Indian epic religious text. He is described as the son of Lord Shiva and the river Goddess Ganga, and is also known as Ganga Putra or Gangadhar. Devabhay is believed to have assumed the form of a serpent to protect the sage Kapila during a cosmic battle.

Another reference to Devabhay can be found in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic, where he is mentioned as one of the warriors in the battle of Kurukshetra. He is described as the king of the Yakshas, and is a powerful warrior on the side of the Pandava army.
